blindSourceSummaries: International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (last updated Mar 2026): same-sex relations legal nationwide, no legal gender recognition, LGBTI organisations can register; surveys show strong support for an anti-discrimination law, but a 2018 poll by a national survey firm found only 22% of the public supported same-sex civil unions and a majority opposed trans women's access to women's toilets; diversity-and-inclusion executive orders (2019, amended 2023) exist but were not implemented as of 2025; non-discrimination ordinances enacted at local-government, city and state/province levels, while a national SOGIE law has been filed repeatedly since 1999 but never passed; a 2013 anti-bullying law and a 2017 education policy (reiterated 2022) cover SOGI in schools; a 2019 safe-spaces law covers homophobic and transphobic slurs.

A national news outlet (26 June 2025): an eighteen-year-old trans woman (a local student) was found dead in a river on 23 June 2025 with visible signs of physical assault; a person who admitted picking her up the previous night surrendered to police and denied killing her; the same piece records the killing of a trans activist and former journalist by an unidentified gunman inside an acupuncture clinic in a southern city (23 June) and of another trans woman in a city earlier in 2025; a national LGBT alliance says the violence proves LGBT people remain unsafe and demands passage of an equality bill, stuck in the national legislature for 25 years (latest version filed 2022).
